subject.title: Feature: Add 'private' groupPolicy option for Slack channels

question: Should Slack private-channel membership be accepted as an opt-in group-message authorization boundary, and should that policy value be scoped to Slack rather than the shared channel `GroupPolicy` contract?
rationale: The code change is clear, but deciding that private Slack channels and private Slack Connect/shared channels are a sufficient trust boundary is a security/product choice that automation should not make.

options.title: Approve Slack-Scoped Private Policy
options.body: Add an opt-in Slack-only private-channel policy and cover normal messages, slash/native commands, action reads, docs, metadata, security audit behavior, and Slack Connect caveats without changing existing defaults.

options.title: Reject Private Channels As A Boundary
options.body: Keep `allowlist` as the required Slack group authorization mode and document why private channels are not sufficient for agent/tool access.

options.title: Defer Behind Broader Slack Authorization Work
options.body: Wait for adjacent Slack sender/member-policy decisions to settle, then revisit whether private-channel policy is still needed.

recommendation.title: Approve Slack-Scoped Private Policy
recommendation.body: Add an opt-in Slack-only private-channel policy and cover normal messages, slash/native commands, action reads, docs, metadata, security audit behavior, and Slack Connect caveats without changing existing defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: They already reviewed this exact issue and have recent history on Slack/channel access-boundary behavior.
